chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh said: Muhammad ibn Hammam informed us from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from al-Rabi' ibn Waddad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you see the crescent of Sha'ban, count twenty-nine nights; if the sky is clear and you do not see it, do not fast, and if it is cloudy, fast."

key_terms.أَصْحَتْ: The sky was clear/clear of clouds
key_terms.هِلَالُ شَعْبَانَ: Crescent of the month of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the crescent moon is not seen on the 29th of Sha'ban due to cloudy weather?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the practical protocol for sighting the Ramadan crescent, distinguishing between clear skies where absence of sighting precludes fasting and cloudy conditions where fasting is obligatory to avoid uncertainty. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on *khusuf* (obscuration) as a valid indicator for completing the month, ensuring the community enters Ramadan with certainty rather than doubt.
